look_here_first: COMMON REED: robust very tall jointed perennial stems, long broad leaves, underground rhizomes and enormous silver-tan feathery panicles. CRITICAL: Phragmites australis includes native North American and invasive introduced lineages. Do not identify lineage from this single photo or decide on treatment without native/introduced subspecies evaluation.

what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole reed stand and rooted rhizome, with habitat
Membranous/hairy ligule, leaf sheath and stem node macros

crew_field_check: Arundo donax (giant reed) has bamboo-like robust stems, frequently wide leaves and different denser seedhead spikelets; Zizaniopsis miliacea (giant cutgrass) is another tall native wetland grass with a more open panicle and different spikelets. To distinguish Phragmites native vs introduced, compare multi-character sheath, leaf, culm and glume traits and ideally genetics/provenance; never a single seedhead.
